prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1392; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed collision in a parking lot. The insured reports that another vehicle backed into the rear of their car while it was parked, and the claimant was seated inside at the time.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force when the incident occurred. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report and two witness statements, which describe the collision the same way the insured did. Photos taken at the scene show the damage is consistent with the reported impact, and the other driver has also confirmed the account.

Entry 4: Reviewed the vehicle damage estimate. The rear bumper, tailgate and taillight damage lines up with the described point of impact, and no prior damage to the vehicle is on record.

Entry 5: Claimant's counsel submitted a demand reporting neck and back strain. The claimant has given the same account of the accident in every conversation so far, and the police and witnesses confirm they were in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 6: Medical records show treatment following a typical course for soft tissue strain, with care tapering as the claimant improved. No prior injury to the neck or back is known, and the reported injury is plausible for a collision of this type.

Entry 7: Reviewed the file with supervisor. Liability and coverage are confirmed, the injury is consistent with the mechanism of the collision, and the claim is moving forward for evaluation of the bodily injury portion.
